findings.citation: spec.md ## Journeys: "its recorded known defect is gone. `docs/journeys.md`'s \"Known defect, scoped to `tenant-scoped-sign-in`\" line is removed as part of this feature."
findings.note: The line still claimed the lookup is by username across all tenants — false once V55 landed. Fixed by the orchestrator, who is the single writer of docs/journeys.md: no implementer or fixer may edit it. Replaced with what the defect was and what removed it.

findings.citation: spec.md ## Journeys: "- **Operate a second tenant safely** (`wanted` → `exists`)"
findings.note: The journey still read `wanted`. Moved to `exists` by the orchestrator, with the proof named: GlobalUsernameIndexMigrationTest, CrossTenantUsernameAgentCreationApiTest, AgentLoginApiTest, TesterUsernameConflictApiTest, and SecondTenantSignInApiTest for legitimate second-Tenant operation.

The new Login glossary entry has no source in any story, Decisions taken entry or ticket — it was decided inside the audit ticket and declared through harness.terms. Documentation rather than behaviour. Left as is: the term is true and useful, and removing it would leave the glossary poorer.

passwordInvalid was removed outright rather than wired to error?.field === 'password' as the reference create-agent-login-dialog.tsx does. Harmless today, since no Tester error targets the password field.

findings.citation: docs/agents/coding-standards.md, Backend rule 2: "Business rules live in the service layer; a controller translates HTTP <-> domain and never branches on domain state."
findings.note: The global-uniqueness pre-check and the flush-time branching on Postgres constraint names sit in the controller. The identical rule lives in a service on the Agent path (AgentLoginService.requireLoginCreatable / toConflict), so a compliant pattern exists in this repository and was not used. The controller's pre-existing primary-contact branch does not license adding more.

Username normalization is expressed four times in three dialects — String.strip() at AgentController:103 and :126 and TesterController:83, JPQL lower(trim(...)) here, SQL lower(btrim(...)) in V55. They are NOT equivalent: Java strip() removes all Unicode whitespace, trim/btrim remove spaces only, so a username padded with a tab or NBSP normalizes differently in Java than in the index. Latent correctness, not merely duplication.

TesterConflictException is a package-private nested class inside the controller, while the AgentLoginConflictException its own Javadoc claims to mirror is a top-level public class in its own file. The @ExceptionHandler body is byte-identical to AgentController's.

Third copy of the SubmitError type plus errorFor() pair, with the USERNAME_TAKEN wording repeated verbatim as a literal (also in create-agent-dialog.tsx and create-agent-login-dialog.tsx). A shared helper beside readErrorCode in lib/api/errors.ts would hold the wording once — which matters because the human chose that exact wording.

Three added tests identical but for the username transformation (identity / toUpperCase / padding). Backend rule 12 does not bind — its trigger is more than two branch conditions — so this is judgement only; a @ParameterizedTest would carry the same coverage.

saveAndFlush runs in a controller method with no @Transactional, so the User insert commits independently of the Tester insert that follows; a failure between them leaves an orphan login row. Not new behaviour and not a rule 3 violation. Fixing F5 by moving the write into a service with a transaction boundary fixes this too.
